changed.title: Sixteen scheduled columns obstruct every shift-12 mate lookup on the four-round 17-bit row zero
changed.statement:
let k : Nat := 17
let rot := fun (s word : Nat) =>
  ((word <<< (s % k)) ||| (word >>> (k - s % k))) % 2 ^ k
let step := fun (word : Nat) =>
  (List.range k).foldl (fun acc b =>
    acc ||| ((xor (word.testBit b)
      (!(word.testBit ((b + 1) % k)) && word.testBit ((b + 2) % k))).toNat <<< b)) 0
let output := fun (w : Nat) =>
  ((List.range 4).foldl (fun x t =>
    step (x ^^^ rot 1 x ^^^ rot (k - 1) x) ^^^ rot (2 * t) w ^^^
      (3 ^ (k + (t + 1)) % 2 ^ k)) (rot 1 w)) >>> 8
let columnPass := fun (key name : Nat) =>
  ((List.range 4).foldl (fun state j =>
    step (state ^^^ rot 2 state ^^^ rot (k - 2) state) ^^^
      rot (3 * (j + 1) + 1) key ^^^ (3 ^ (k + (4 + (j + 1))) % 2 ^ k))
    (rot 3 key ^^^ name)) < 2 ^ 8
let keys := List.range (2 ^ k)
∀ lookup : Nat → Bool, ∃ column : Fin (2 ^ k),
  column.val ∈ ([0, 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22, 26, 29] : List Nat) ∧
  ¬ ((∃ w ∈ keys, output w = 0 ∧ columnPass w column.val) ↔
    (∃ candidate ∈ keys,
      (if candidate.testBit 2 then output candidate = 0
       else lookup (output (candidate ^^^ 12)) = true) ∧ columnPass candidate column.val))
changed.unlocks: Determines whether the checked shift-12 mate conflict forces a wrong answer on an actual scheduled graph column, even after all other witness keys are included.
changed.context: Use positive column 0 and negative columns 1, 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10, 11, 12, 14, 15, 18, 22, 26, 29. The closed computation at 173a4e370 in notes/seat-rlift-1/output-labels/Shift12ColumnMasks.lean verifies four mask tests. Interpret each bit at its scalar key by induction on the packed recurrence. Read coversNames by induction on the nine remaining planes. If the lookup accepts an available name at 0, that name also accepts a negative column. If it accepts none, there is no direct probed witness and column 0 is wrongly rejected.

changed.title: Exact weighted average support of binary parity contradictions when deleting any one equation preserves inconsistency
changed.statement:
∀ (n m : ℕ) (row : Fin m → Fin n → ZMod 2) (rhs : Fin m → ZMod 2),
  let ok := fun (rows : Finset (Fin m)) => ∃ x : Fin n → ZMod 2,
    ∀ e ∈ rows, (∑ j, row e j * x j) = rhs e
  let W := Finset.univ.filter (fun indices : Finset (Fin m) =>
    (∀ j : Fin n, indices.sum (fun e => row e j) = 0) ∧ indices.sum rhs = 1)
  ¬ ok Finset.univ → (∀ e : Fin m, ¬ ok (Finset.univ.erase e)) →
    W.Nonempty ∧
    (∀ e ∈ W.biUnion id, 2*(W.filter (fun subset => e ∈ subset)).card = W.card) ∧
    ∀ w : Fin m → ℕ,
      2*W.sum (fun support => support.sum w) = W.card * (W.biUnion id).sum w ∧
      ∃ D ∈ W, 2*D.sum w ≤ (W.biUnion id).sum w
changed.unlocks: halves the total weight needed for an odd binary dependency when every single row deletion preserves inconsistency
changed.context: Deletion of coordinate e supplies a contradiction avoiding e by the binary solvability criterion. If e occurs, also pick one containing it. Their symmetric difference has zero left and right sums and contains e. Toggling this difference pairs all contradictions containing e with those avoiding it. Sum the coordinate counts against the weights and select a member of at most the average weight.
